articles.title: Patterson Signs For Torino
articles.excerpt: Nathan Patterson has left Everton, signing for Serie A club Torino on a permanent deal for an undisclosed fee. The 24-year-old full-back joined the Blues from Rangers in January 2022, playing 68 times for the Club across all competitions. Patterson made his Toffees debut in an FA Cup fifth-round victory over Boreham Wood in March 2022, and the following year, played 19 Premier League matches in his first full season on Merseyside. A highlight of that campaign arrived when the young Scot started in Everton’s emphatic 5-1 victory at Brighton & Hove Albion in May 2023, when Patterson excellently tamed tricky winger Kaoru Mitoma. On the international stage, the defender helped Scotland qualify for this summer’s 2026 FIFA World Cup finals, where he earned caps against Haiti, Morocco and Brazil. Everyone at Everton thanks Nathan for his commitment to the Club across the past four-and-a-half years and wishes him all the best for the next step in his career.

articles.title: Campbell Joins MK Dons On Loan
articles.excerpt: Everton Under-21s defender Eli Campbell has signed for League One club MK Dons on loan. Campbell – an England Under-20s international – joined the Blues’ Academy in 2017 and signed his first professional contract with the Club five years later. The 22-year-old got his first loan experience with Fleetwood Town for the second half of the 2023/24 season, moving to Scottish side Ross County the following campaign. Campbell was rewarded with a two-year deal at Everton and made his maiden appearance at Hill Dickinson Stadium in January 2026 during Everton’s FA Cup tie with Sunderland. Another loan move to League One followed, with Campbell going on to make 13 league starts for Port Vale last term. He now links up with Paul Warne’s MK Dons, who played out a goalless draw with Leicester City on Saturday.

While initial diagnoses suggested a minor knock, subsequent scans revealed significant cartilage damage requiring surgery. articles.title: Under-17s off to winning start in Premier League Cup
articles.excerpt: AFC Bournemouth under-17s got off to a winning start in the U17 Premier League Cup, thanks to a 3-2 victory over Southampton. Goals from Leyland Waite, Denzel Decardi-Nelson and Fikayo Solanke secured the three points for the Cherries. It ensures the Cherries get off to the strongest possible start in a group that also contains Chelsea and West Ham United. After the game, under-18s assistant coach, Elliot Head, spoke to afcb.co.uk: "The first half was a tight game with chances for both teams. "We regained the ball high up the pitch a few teams that lead to some good chances which we weren't quite able to capitalise from." The Cherries went into the interval level at 0-0, after tight first-half. Scoring in the 50th and 55th minute, the Cherries were then forced back into their own half, as Southampton brought the score level. The winner came in the 88th minute and secured all three points for the Cherries. Head continued: "The lads showed fantastic attitude throughout the game and had to dig deep after coming off the back of four games in ten days." The next under-17 cup game is away at Chelsea on 15th September.

Our Young Whites have had no problems finding the back of the net in the first few games of the season, but we struck the perfect balance here, with a clean sheet to boot. Quashie doubled his tally immediately after the interval, before Trialist Jose Sani scored for a third straight game with seven minutes to play. Michael Allen saved a penalty late on to cap off a complete away day display. Newcastle proved tricky opponents at Whitley Park last season, winning 3-0 in this fixture back in February, and we had an early scare as the dangerous Trevan Sanusi rattled the crossbar with a thunderous effort. articles.title: Under-18s looking to "bounce back" after defeat to Ipswich
articles.excerpt: AFC Bournemouth under-18s Lead Coach, James Lowy, says his side will "bounce back" after a 6-2 defeat away at Ipswich Town. Goals from a trialist and Harley Simpson saw the Cherries go into half-time level at 2-2, before Ipswich secured the three points in the second-half. James Lowy spoke to afcb.co.uk: "It was a game of two halves. I thought we competed really well in the first-half and put ourselves in a good position. "We created a number of opportunities through pressing and regaining the ball high, but we didn't capitalise on those opportunities. "For us to compete at this level, they are chances that we would need to take. "In the second-half, we struggled to compete in our duels. In and around the final third we lacked some quality and could have done better with some chances too. "Ipswich defended well, and the difference was in both boxes today. "It's been a really tough period for us physically, with games coming thick and fast. "We have a young squad and some injures, so it is important for us now to rest and recover and put ourselves in the best position going into West Ham on Saturday." Lowy's players are back in action this Saturday (5th September).

The Cherries will welcome the Imps to Vitality Stadium, with kick-off scheduled for 7.45pm and the fixture set to be broadcast live on Sky Sports+. The tie will mark AFC Bournemouth’s first appearance in this season’s competition, having entered at the third-round stage due to the club’s involvement in the UEFA Europa League. Lincoln arrive on the south coast having earned promotion to the Sky Bet Championship last season, returning to the second tier of English football for the first time in 65 years. The Imps booked their place in the third round after progressing through the opening stages of the competition, beating Derby County 2-1 at Pride Park in round one before winning their second round tie at Blackpool 4-1. The two sides last met competitively during the 2009/10 League Two campaign, a season which ultimately saw the Cherries earn promotion to League One. articles.excerpt: AFC Bournemouth has agreed a new three-year partnership with Thatchers Cider, with the Somerset-based producer becoming the club's Official Cider Supplier. The agreement represents the first official cider partnership in the club's history and will see Thatchers products served throughout Vitality Stadium, further enhancing the matchday experience for supporters. Thatchers Gold will headline the cider offering across the stadium, complemented by Thatchers Zero to provide supporters with both alcoholic and alcohol-free options. The collaboration also marks a significant step for Thatchers, adding a flagship football partnership to an established portfolio spanning cricket and rugby, while supporting AFC Bournemouth as the club continues to grow on and off the pitch. The Shuttle Bus will run for each Coventry City home league match, and the cost to fans will continue to be subsidised by the Football Club as it helps its supporters travel to the Coventry Building Society Arena on matchdays. The return service will be priced just £5 each matchday, with fans able to buy their ticket as they board the Shuttle Bus pre-match. A member of staff will take contactless card payments (no cash payment) and issue a return shuttle bus ticket. Post-match, fans will just need to show driver their shuttle ticket for the return journey back into the city centre. Please note that a ‘one-way’ ticket is not available and buses will not be taking payments post-match. The service will collect fans ahead of matches from the Bus Interchange at Coventry Train Station (near Central Six, opposite Burger King) and then pick up fans at White Street Coach Park, before dropping them off at the Bus Station at Arena Park Shopping Centre, near to Foleshill Road/Nandos. articles.excerpt: AFC Bournemouth’s defence of the FA Women’s National League Cup started with defeat in their opening group game against Moneyfields at the John Jenkins Stadium on Thursday. The Cherries memorably lifted the cup after beating Southern Premier Division counterparts Plymouth Argyle in the final at QPR’s Matrade Loftus Road headquarters in March 2026. But the holders were beaten 3-1 by Division One South West leaders Moneyfields thanks to strikes from Tierney Scott and Sophie Phelps, coupled with an unfortunate own goal from Clarabella Hall. Tilly Westcott, Isla Betts and Mia Hammick were all named in the Cherries starting line-up, the trio all products of the club’s successful development programme. They had mixed fortunes with Westcott and Hammick both impressing, while Betts succumbed to an injury midway through the first half. Westcott capped an excellent individual display by netting the Cherries’ goal, the young midfielder finishing superbly from distance to make it 2-1 early in the second half. articles.title: Akinmboni joins Dundee on season-long loan
articles.excerpt: AFC Bournemouth defender Matai Akinmboni has joined Scottish Premiership side Dundee on a season-long loan. The 19-year-old American centre-back moves to Dens Park for the 2026/27 campaign as he continues his development with regular first-team football. Akinmboni joined the Cherries from Major League Soccer outfit DC United in January 2025, signing with the club after making his senior debut for the Washington-based side at just 15 years and 328 days. A United States youth international, Akinmboni progressed through DC United's academy before establishing himself as one of the youngest players to appear in MLS. The move to Dundee will provide Akinmboni with the opportunity to gain further experience of senior football in the Scottish Premiership, with the defender joining a Dundee squad that also includes former Cherries player Owen Bevan. Bevan completed a permanent move to Dundee from Bournemouth this summer. Akinmboni will now link up with his former Cherries team-mate as Dundee continue their 2026/27 Scottish Premiership campaign.
